title: Primary-Archive Reference Catalog of Hugo Riemann (1849-1919) and Its Strictly Separated Precursor & Formalization Lineage
purpose: Provides a strictly separated, primary-archive-verified bibliography of Karl Wilhelm Julius Hugo Riemann's theoretical, systematic, historical, lexicographical, analytical, and editorial oeuvre (1870-1919), cleanly isolated from Bernhard Riemann's analytic number theory (formulary_lineage_v1.json) and differential geometry, and explicitly separating Hugo Riemann's own writings from historical precursors and 20th/21st-century Neo-Riemannian mathematical formalizations.

subject.discipline: Musicology, music theory (harmonic dualism, Funktionstheorie, Schritte/Wechsel, rhythm/meter/phrasing, Tonvorstellungen), lexicography, paleography
subject.authority_citation: Arntz, Michael (2003). Riemann, Karl Wilhelm Julius Hugo. In Neue Deutsche Biographie (NDB), Vol. 21, pp. 592-594.

disciplines: RIEM-A: Analytic number theory (1859 zeta function, explicit formula, Riemann Hypothesis -> Ergentics1/Riemannian & formulary_lineage_v1.json)
RIEM-B: Differential geometry (1854/1868 smooth manifolds, metric tensor, curvature)
distinct_from.authority_citation: Ullrich, Peter (2003). Riemann, Georg Friedrich Bernhard. In Neue Deutsche Biographie (NDB), Vol. 21, pp. 591-592; Cantor, Moritz (1889). Allgemeine Deutsche Biographie (ADB), Vol. 28, pp. 555-559.

disambiguation_header.non_conflation_rule: Entries in this vault belong exclusively to RIEM-C (Hugo Riemann music theory and its typed formalization lineage). No entry may be merged into formulary_lineage_v1.json (RIEM-A) or treated as part of Bernhard Riemann's differential geometry (RIEM-B). Any cross-tradition bridge (e.g., discrete Tonnetz graphs embedded in continuous voice-leading orbifolds) must carry provenance_role='geometric_orbifold_bridge' and explicit namespace separation.

archival_coverage_note.nachlass_status: Hugo Riemann's personal Nachlass was destroyed in a 1943 wartime air raid in Leipzig (NDB 21, 2003); no complete critical Werkverzeichnis exists covering all ~50+ monographs, >200 journal essays, >70 critical/phrasing editions, and ~70 compositions (op. 1-69).
archival_coverage_note.primary_catalog_baseline: Carl Mennicke (ed.), Riemann-Festschrift (1909, pp. xxv-xl) enumerates 58 monographs plus categorized essays, editions, and compositions through 1909; post-1909 final-decade works (1909-1919) are verified via Deutsche Biographie (NDB 21), UPenn/HathiTrust digitized catalogs, BSB Munich MDZ, Internet Archive originals, and Cambridge/Oxford University Press primary bibliographies.
archival_coverage_note.source_standard: Primary digitized archives, national library authority records, university presses, and peer-reviewed journals only (zero crowdsourced encyclopedia sources).

categories.name: Foundational Harmonic, Acoustic, Logical & Cognitive Works (1870-1917)
categories.focus: Harmonic dualism (Oberklang/Unterklang), Schritte/Wechsel transformational syntax, tonal function theory (Funktionstheorie: T/S/D), modulation, the 1905 pivot away from physical undertones, and late cognitive Tonvorstellungen.

categories.name: Rhythm, Meter, Phrasing, Dynamics/Agogics, Counterpoint & Composition (1876-1913)
categories.focus: Anacrustic (Auftakt) metric theory, 8-measure hierarchical phrase archetypes (Achttaktigkeit), agogic/dynamic phrasing, counterpoint, aesthetics, and the 3-volume Grosse Kompositionslehre.

categories.name: Historical Musicology, Paleography, Theory History & Comparative Tonality (1878-1916)
categories.focus: History of notation, Byzantine neumes, musica ficta, history of music theory (9th-19th c.), multi-volume Handbuch der Musikgeschichte, disciplinary Grundriss der Musikwissenschaft, and folkloric pentatonic/tetrachordal tonality.

categories.name: Musik-Lexikon, Opern-Handbuch, Collected Essays & Complete Max Hesse Katechismen/Handbuecher (1882-1919)
categories.focus: Reference lexicography (Musik-Lexikon eds. 1-9, Opern-Handbuch), collected essays (Praeludien und Studien), and the complete systematic pedagogical encyclopedia of Max Hesse Katechismen/Handbuecher.

categories.name: Analytical Monographs, Historical Monument Editions, Phrasing Editions & Revisions (1883-1919)
categories.focus: Analytical guides (Beethoven string quartets & complete piano sonatas), Mannheim School & early-music critical editions (DTB/DDT/Collegium Musicum), phrasing editions, Thayer/Marx/Gevaert/Widor revisions, plus Mennicke's 1909 primary Festschrift catalog.

categories.name: Strictly Separated Precursors, Neo-Riemannian Algebraic Formalizers, Critical Scholarship & Orbifold Bridge
categories.focus: Explicitly tagged non-Hugo-authored works: mathematical/theoretical precursors (Euler, Hauptmann, Oettingen), group-theoretic Neo-Riemannian formalizations (Lewin, Klumpenhouwer, Hyer, Cohn, Douthett-Steinbach, Gollin, Hook, Fiore-Satyendra, Crans-Fiore-Satyendra), critical historiography (Burnham, Harrison, Mooney, Arntz, Rehding, Probst), and the continuous orbifold bridge linking RIEM-C to RIEM-B (Tymoczko, Callender-Quinn-Tymoczko, Yust).

entries.title: Aesthetische Essays ueber das Dreikunstwerk
entries.publication_details: Neue Zeitschrift fuer Musik 66 (1870), pp. 93-95, 197-199, 320-321.
entries.core_content: Earliest published theoretical essays written under the pseudonym Hugibert Ries, engaging Wagnerian aesthetics prior to Riemann's 1871 Leipzig conservatory studies.

entries.title: Musikalische Logik & Ueber Tonalitaet
entries.publication_details: Neue Zeitschrift fuer Musik 68 (1872), nos. 28-29 & 36-38, pp. 279-282, 353-355, 363-364, 373-374; repr. in Praeludien und Studien, Vol. 3 (1901), pp. 1-22.
entries.core_content: First programmatic articulation of harmonic cadence logic (thesis-antithesis-synthesis: T-S-D-T) and tonality immediately after encountering Arthur von Oettingen's dualism (1866).

entries.title: Ueber das musikalische Hoeren (Goettingen Ph.D. diss., 1873) / Musikalische Logik: Hauptzuege der physiologischen und psychologischen Begruendung unseres Musiksystems
entries.publication_details: Dissertation accepted Goettingen 1873 (Hermann Lotze & Eduard Krueger); printed Leipzig: Druck von F. Andrae's Nachfolger, 1874; trade edition Leipzig: C. F. Kahnt, 1873/1874.
entries.core_content: Doctoral foundation integrating physiological acoustics and Lotzean psychology to derive major/minor consonance, cadential closure, and the logical necessity of harmonic relationships.

entries.title: Die objective Existenz der Untertoene in der Schallwelle
entries.publication_details: Allgemeine deutsche Musikzeitung 2 (1875), pp. 205-206, 213-215; also separate brochure Kassel, 1875.
entries.core_content: Early experimental attempt to demonstrate physical undertones (Untertoene) symmetric to overtones; formally retracted by Riemann himself in 1905 (HR-T13) while keeping logical dualism intact.

entries.title: Die Huelfsmittel der Modulation
entries.publication_details: Kassel, 1875 (cited in Riemann-Festschrift 1909 Werkverzeichnis).
entries.core_content: Early systematic survey of pivot-chord and chromatic modulatory mechanisms preceding the 1887 Systematische Modulationslehre.

entries.title: Musikalische Syntaxis: Grundriss einer harmonischen Satzbildungslehre
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel, 1877 (xvi + 123 pp.; repr. Niederwalluf: Saendig, 1971).
entries.core_content: Introduces the transformational taxonomy of Harmonieschritte: mode-preserving Schritte (Quintschritt, Terzschritt, Leittonschritt, etc.) and mode-inverting Wechsel (Seitenwechsel, Leittonwechsel, Quintwechsel, Terzwechsel) acting on dual major/minor Klaenge.

entries.title: Skizze einer neuen Methode der Harmonielehre (1880) -> Handbuch der Harmonielehre (2nd-6th eds., 1887-1917)
entries.publication_details: 1st ed. Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel, 1880; 2nd ed. as Handbuch der Harmonielehre, 1887; 3rd completely reworked ed. with final function notation, 1898; 6th ed. 1917; French trans. Manuel de l'Harmonie, 1902.
entries.core_content: Riemann's flagship harmony textbook across six lifetime editions, evolving from dual Klang-cipher notation (1880/1887) into the mature canonical functional system (from 3rd ed. 1898 onward).

entries.title: Die Natur der Harmonik (English trans. J. C. Fillmore: The Nature of Harmony, 1886)
entries.publication_details: Paul Graf Waldersee (ed.), Sammlung musikalischer Vortraege, Vol. 4 (Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel, 1882), pp. 159-190; English trans. John Comfort Fillmore, Philadelphia: Theodore Presser, 1886 (also New Lessons in Harmony, 1887).
entries.core_content: Concise public manifesto of harmonic dualism and its earliest direct introduction into English-language music theory.

entries.title: Systematische Modulationslehre als Grundlage der musikalischen Formenlehre
entries.publication_details: Hamburg: J. F. Richter, 1887.
entries.core_content: Links systematic modulation across harmonic space directly to large-scale musical form via functional reinterpretation of chords across tonic centers.

entries.title: Wie hoeren wir Musik? Drei Vortraege (later: Grundlinien der Musik-Aesthetik)
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesse, 1888; expanded editions as Wie hoeren wir Musik? Grundlinien der Musik-Aesthetik (1911, 1919, 1921, 1923).
entries.core_content: Establishes active mental listening as the unifying epistemological premise of Riemann's system: music is constituted by cognitive synthesis of pitch relations and rhythmic-metric grouping.

entries.title: Die Neugestaltung der Harmonielehre
entries.publication_details: Musikalisches Wochenblatt 22 (1891), pp. 513-514, 529-531, 541-543.
entries.core_content: Programmatic announcement of the transition from figured-bass / scale-degree Roman numerals to explicit tonal-function notation (T, S, D).

entries.title: Vereinfachte Harmonielehre oder die Lehre von den tonalen Funktionen der Akkorde (English trans. H. Bewerunge: Harmony Simplified, 1895/1896)
entries.publication_details: London & New York: Augener & Co., 1893 (German original); English trans. Rev. H. Bewerunge as Harmony Simplified, or The Theory of the Tonal Functions of Chords, London: Augener, 1895/1896.
entries.core_content: Foundational treatise of Funktionstheorie: reduces all harmonic events within a key to equivalence classes of three primary tonal functions — Tonic (T / °T), Subdominant (S / °S), and Dominant (D / °D) — plus Scheinkonsonanzen (parallel Tp/Sp/Dp and Leittonwechselklang substitutions).

entries.title: Das Problem des harmonischen Dualismus
entries.publication_details: Neue Zeitschrift fuer Musik 72 [Vol. 101] (1905), nos. 1-4, pp. 3-5, 23-26, 43-46, 67-70.
entries.core_content: Decisive methodological pivot: following Oettingen, Lotze, and Stumpf, Riemann explicitly abandons physical undertone acoustics (and even overtone-only foundations) as irrelevant, re-grounding major/minor polarity strictly in psychological-logical symmetry and interval proportions.

entries.title: Elementar-Schulbuch der Harmonielehre
entries.publication_details: Mainz: B. Schott's Soehne, 1906; later Berlin: Max Hesse, 1919.
entries.core_content: Condensed pedagogical presentation of Riemann's mature post-1905 functional harmony curriculum.

entries.title: Spontane Phantasietatigkeit und verstandesmaessige Arbeit in der tonkuenstlerischen Produktion
entries.publication_details: Jahrbuch der Musikbibliothek Peters 16 (1909), pp. 33-46.
entries.core_content: Analyzes the interplay between spontaneous musical imagination and formal structural reasoning in composition, anticipating the Tonvorstellungen treatises.

entries.title: Ideen zu einer 'Lehre von den Tonvorstellungen' (English annotated trans. R. W. Wason & E. W. Marvin, 1992)
entries.publication_details: Jahrbuch der Musikbibliothek Peters 21/22 (1914/15, pub. 1916), pp. 1-26; annotated English trans. Robert W. Wason & Elizabeth West Marvin, Journal of Music Theory 36(1) (1992), pp. 69-117.
entries.core_content: Crowning late theoretical manifesto: music exists primarily in mental Tone-Imaginations (Tonvorstellungen) governed by the principle of greatest economy (Prinzip der groesstmoeglichen Oekonomie); presents the mature Tabelle der Tonverwandtschaften (Tonnetz) as a cognitive coordinate map of fifth- and third-relations.

entries.title: Neue Beitraege zu einer Lehre von den Tonvorstellungen
entries.publication_details: Jahrbuch der Musikbibliothek Peters 23 (1916, pub. 1917), pp. 1-21.
entries.core_content: Extends the cognitive Tonvorstellungen framework into rhythm and meter: contrasts binary symmetry (Aufstellung/Antwort, proposta/risposta, 2x2x2 grouping) against triple metric weight trajectories (Schwer-Leicht-Schwer) and spatial accumulation (Ansammeln) of motives in memory.

entries.title: Vademecum fuer den ersten Klavierunterricht (1876) & Elementar-Musiklehre (1883)
entries.publication_details: Vademecum: Leipzig, 1876; Elementar-Musiklehre: Hamburg: K. Graedener & J. F. Richter, 1883.
entries.core_content: Foundational pedagogical manuals reforming elementary notation literacy and keyboard instruction around harmonic and rhythmic comprehension.

entries.title: Neue Schule der Melodik: Entwurf einer Lehre des Contrapunkts nach einer gaenzlich neuen Methode
entries.publication_details: Hamburg: Karl Graedener & J. F. Richter, 1883.
entries.core_content: Derives melodic motion and counterpoint from underlying harmonic progression and metric weight rather than isolated species rules.

entries.title: Vergleichende theoretisch-praktische Klavier-Schule, Op. 39 (Comparative Pianoforte School)
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Fr. Kistner, 1883 (Part 1 System, Part 2 Method); later Hamburg/St. Petersburg: D. Rahter (1901, 1912); bilingual ed. with J. C. Fillmore, Milwaukee: Rohlfing, 1887.
entries.core_content: Integrates keyboard technique with ear training, polyphonic phrasing, and harmonic analysis; praised by Hans von Buelow (quoted in Riemann-Festschrift 1909).

entries.title: Musikalische Dynamik und Agogik: Lehrbuch der musikalischen Phrasirung auf Grund einer Revision der Lehre von der musikalischen Metrik und Rhythmik
entries.publication_details: Hamburg & St. Petersburg: D. Rahter, 1884.
entries.core_content: Establishes agogic accent (subtle micro-temporal lengthening of metric focal points) and dynamic shading as objective structural correlates of phrasing and anacrustic (upbeat-to-downbeat) motive boundaries.

entries.title: Praktische Anleitung zum Phrasieren (English trans.: Practical Guide to the Art of Phrasing, 1890)
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesse, 1886; English trans. New York: G. Schirmer, 1890.
entries.core_content: Operational manual detailing explicit phrasing-mark placement through complete thematic, harmonic, and rhythmic analysis of Classical and Romantic works.

entries.title: Lehrbuch des einfachen, doppelten und imitierenden Kontrapunkts (English trans. S. H. Lovewell, 1904)
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel, 1888; English trans. S. Harrison Lovewell as Text-book of Simple and Double Counterpoint Including Imitation or Canon, Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel, 1904.
entries.core_content: Systematic treatise on simple, invertible (double), and imitative/canonic counterpoint grounded in harmonic function and metric placement.

entries.title: Die Elemente der musikalischen Aesthetik (French trans. G. Humbert: Les elements de l'esthetique musicale, 1906)
entries.publication_details: Berlin & Stuttgart: W. Spemann, 1900; French trans. Georges Humbert, Paris: F. Alcan, 1906.
entries.core_content: Formalizes the distinction between expressive content (pitch/loudness/tempo trajectories) and teachable form (harmony, rhythm/meter), introducing the distinction between 'living' intra-motive melodic steps and 'dead' inter-motive intervals.

entries.title: Grosse Kompositionslehre (3 Volumes, 1902-1913)
entries.publication_details: Berlin & Stuttgart: W. Spemann — Bd. I: Der homophone Satz (Melodielehre und Harmonielehre), 1902; Bd. II: Der polyphone Satz (Kontrapunkt, Fuge und Kanon), 1903; Bd. III: Der Orchestersatz und der dramatische Gesangstil, 1913.
entries.core_content: Comprehensive three-volume synthesis unifying Riemann's harmonic, melodic, metric, contrapuntal, orchestral, and dramatic composition theories.

entries.title: System der musikalischen Rhythmik und Metrik
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel, 1903 (repr. Niederwalluf: Saendig, 1971).
entries.core_content: Definitive codification of Riemannian metric theory: end-accented binary hierarchy (light-heavy / Auftakt-Schwerpunkt), the normative 8-measure period (Achttaktigkeit, 2^3 hierarchy), and systematic period-transformation rules (contraction/elision, expansion, appendage, repetition).

entries.title: Studien zur Geschichte der Notenschrift
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel, 1878 (Habilitationsschrift, Universitaet Leipzig).
entries.core_content: Riemann's Leipzig Habilitation thesis opening his historical-paleographical research into alphabetic, neumatic, tablature, and mensural music notation systems.

entries.title: Die Entwickelung unserer Notenschrift
entries.publication_details: Paul Graf Waldersee (ed.), Sammlung musikalischer Vortraege, Vol. 3 (Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel, 1881).
entries.core_content: Compact synthesis tracing the structural evolution of Western staff and rhythmic notation.

entries.title: Geschichte der Musiktheorie im IX.-XIX. Jahrhundert (English trans. R. Haggh, 1962 [Books I-II] & W. C. Mickelsen, 1977 [Book III])
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesse, 1898; 2nd ed. rev. Gustav Becking, Berlin: Max Hesse, 1920/21; repr. Hildesheim: Georg Olms, 1990; English trans. Books I-II Raymond H. Haggh (History of Music Theory, Lincoln: Univ. of Nebraska Press, 1962); Book III William C. Mickelsen (Hugo Riemann's Theory of Harmony, Lincoln: Univ. of Nebraska Press, 1977).
entries.core_content: Landmark 1,000-year history of Western music theory from medieval organum and counterpoint (Books I-II) through Zarlino, Rameau, Tartini, Hauptmann, and Oettingen to Riemann's own harmonic dualism and function theory (Book III).

entries.title: Geschichte der Musik seit Beethoven (1800-1900)
entries.publication_details: Berlin & Stuttgart: W. Spemann, 1901.
entries.core_content: Comprehensive historiographical survey of nineteenth-century music, style periods, and chromatic harmonic expansion.

entries.title: Ueber Japanische Musik (& Sechs originale chinesische und japanische Melodien)
entries.publication_details: Musikalisches Wochenblatt 33 (1902), pp. 209-210, 229-231, 245-246, 257-259, 273-274, 289-290; accompanying edition Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel, 1902.
entries.core_content: Early comparative-musicology study testing Riemann's latent-tonality and pentatonic-scale models on East Asian melodies (contrasting with the Berlin phonograph school of Stumpf and Hornbostel).

entries.title: Handbuch der Musikgeschichte (2 Volumes in 5 Parts, 1904-1913)
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel — Bd. I.1 Altertum und Mittelalter [Antike] (1904); Bd. I.2 Die Musik des Mittelalters bis 1450 (1905); Bd. II.1 Das Zeitalter der Renaissance bis 1600 (1907); Bd. II.2 Das Generalbasszeitalter: Die Monodie des 17. Jh. (1912); Bd. II.3 Die Musik des 18. und 19. Jh. (1913); 2nd ed. rev. Alfred Einstein (1919-1922).
entries.core_content: Monumental five-part general history of Western music structured around compositional style principles (Stilprinzipien), accompanied monody, and the historical emergence of the Mannheim/Classical instrumental style.

entries.title: Verloren gegangene Selbstverstaendlichkeiten in der Musik des 15.-16. Jahrhunderts: Die musica ficta, eine Ehrenrettung
entries.publication_details: Langensalza: Hermann Beyer & Soehne, 1907.
entries.core_content: Historical-theoretical reconstruction of unnotated Renaissance chromatic inflection (musica ficta) via implicit leading-tone and cadence laws.

entries.title: Kleines Handbuch der Musikgeschichte mit Periodisierung nach Stilprinzipien und Formen
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel, 1908 (later eds. 1919, 1922, 1947).
entries.core_content: Compact single-volume historical taxonomy periodizing Western music by formal and contrapuntal/harmonic style principles rather than biography.

entries.title: Grundriss der Musikwissenschaft
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Quelle & Meyer, 1908; 2nd ed. 1914; 3rd ed. 1919; 4th ed. rev. Johannes Wolf, 1928.
entries.core_content: Programmatic disciplinary architecture of Musikwissenschaft (acoustics, tone physiology/psychology, aesthetics, music theory/composition, and music history) parallel to Guido Adler's 1885 division.

entries.title: Die byzantinische Notenschrift im 10. bis 15. Jahrhundert (1909), Studien zur byzantinischen Musik (1909), & Neue Beitraege zur Loesung der Probleme der byzantinischen Notenschrift (1915)
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel, 1909 (monograph + Studien); Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel, 1915 (polemic with H. J. W. Tillyard).
entries.core_content: Decipherment studies of medieval Byzantine neumatic notation and intervallic transcription (historically superseded in part by Tillyard/Wellesz, demonstrating empirical falsifiability of paleographic hypotheses).

entries.title: Folkloristische Tonalitaetsstudien. I: Pentatonik und tetrachordale Melodik im schottischen, irischen, walisischen, skandinavischen und spanischen Volksliede und im gregorianischen Gesange
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel, 1916.
entries.core_content: Late comparative melodic study analyzing Celtic, Scandinavian, Spanish folk songs and Gregorian chant through pentatonic fifth-chains, tetrachordal frames, and pien-tone modulatory links (analyzed in Gelbart & Rehding 2011).

entries.authors: Hugo Riemann (9th ed. completed by Alfred Einstein, 1919)
entries.title: Musik-Lexikon (1st-9th eds., 1882-1919; English: Dictionary of Music, trans. J. S. Shedlock, 1893-1908; French: Dictionnaire de musique, trans. G. Humbert, 1899/1913)
entries.publication_details: 1st ed. Leipzig: Verlag des Bibliographischen Instituts, 1882 (1036 pp.); 2nd ed. 1884; 3rd-8th eds. Leipzig/Berlin: Max Hesse (1887, 1894, 1900, 1905, 1909, 1916); 9th ed. ed. Alfred Einstein, Berlin: Max Hesse, 1919; English trans. J. S. Shedlock, London: Augener (1896, 4th ed. 1908).
entries.core_content: Single-author encyclopedic dictionary of music theory, history, instruments, and biography that standardized modern German musicological terminology and served as the primary definitions glossary across nine lifetime editions.

entries.title: Opern-Handbuch: Repertorium der dramatisch-musikalischen Litteratur
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: C. A. Koch, 1887-[1893] (with supplements).
entries.core_content: Structured bibliographic repertory of operas, operettas, ballets, oratorios, and dramatic cantatas designed as a supplement to every music lexicon.

entries.title: Praeludien und Studien: Gesammelte Aufsaetze zur Aesthetik, Theorie und Geschichte der Musik (3 Volumes, 1895-1901)
entries.publication_details: Vol. 1: Frankfurt a. M.: H. Bechhold, 1895; Vols. 2-3: Leipzig: Hermann Seemann Nachfolger, 1900-1901 (repr. Hildesheim: Georg Olms, 1967).
entries.core_content: Three-volume collected essays preserving key theoretical papers including 'Das chromatische Tonsystem' (Vol. 1, pp. 183-219), 'Musikalische Logik' (Vol. 3, pp. 1-22), 'Zur Theorie von Konsonanz und Dissonanz' (Vol. 3, pp. 31-46), and 'Hie Wagner! Hie Schumann!' (Vol. 3, pp. 204-214).

entries.title: Katechismus der Musik (Allgemeine Musiklehre) -> Allgemeine Musiklehre: Handbuch der Musik
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesse, 1888 (Max Hesses illustrierte Katechismen, Bd. 5); later editions through 1918/1922 as Allgemeine Musiklehre.
entries.core_content: Opening volume of the Max Hesse Katechismen/Handbuecher encyclopedia summarizing notation, intervals, scales, meter, rhythm, and basic harmony.

entries.title: Katechismus der Musikgeschichte (2 Parts, 1888-1889) -> Abriss der Musikgeschichte (English: Catechism of Musical History, 1892)
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesse, 1888-1889 (later eds. 1901, 1906, 1909, 1914, 1919); English trans. London: Augener, 1892.
entries.core_content: Two-part handbook covering historical instruments/tone-systems (Part 1) and eras of musical composition (Part 2).

entries.title: Katechismus der Musikinstrumente (Kleine Instrumentationslehre) -> Handbuch der Musikinstrumente
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesse, 1888 (later eds. 1897, 1904, 1908, 1919, 1920); English trans. Catechism of Musical Instruments, London: Augener, 1888/1890.
entries.core_content: Organological and acoustic classification of orchestral and keyboard instruments.

entries.title: Katechismus der Orgel (Orgellehre) -> Handbuch der Orgel
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesse, 1888 (later eds. 1910, 1919).
entries.core_content: Organ construction, acoustics, registration, and liturgical/concert literature (rooted in Riemann's 1878-80 Leipzig organ lectures).

entries.title: Katechismus des Klavierspiels -> Handbuch des Klavierspiels (English: Catechism of Pianoforte Playing, 1892)
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesse, 1888 (later eds. 1897, 1905, 1916); English trans. London: Augener, 1892.
entries.core_content: Pedagogical handbook codifying touch, pedaling, phrasing, and polyphonic keyboard execution.

entries.title: Katechismus der Kompositionslehre (2 Parts) -> Grundriss der Kompositionslehre (Musikalische Formenlehre)
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesse, 1889; retitled Grundriss der Kompositionslehre (Musikalische Formenlehre), 1897, 1905, 1916, 1922.
entries.core_content: Concise systematic Formenlehre covering song forms, rondo, variation, sonata form, and polyphonic genres.

entries.title: Katechismus des Generalbass-Spiels -> Anleitung zum Generalbass-Spielen (Harmonie-Uebungen am Klavier)
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesse, 1889; later eds. 1903, 1909, 1917.
entries.core_content: Bridges historical basso continuo realization with Riemannian functional harmony so students master both Baroque figured bass and functional analysis.

entries.title: Katechismus des Musik-Diktats -> Handbuch des Musik-Diktats (Systematische Gehoersbildung)
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesse, 1889; later eds. 1904, 1916.
entries.core_content: Systematic ear-training method translating auditory perception into metric, harmonic-functional, and contrapuntal transcription.

entries.title: Katechismus der Harmonielehre (1890) -> Katechismus / Handbuch der Harmonie- und Modulationslehre
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesse, 1890; retitled Katechismus der Harmonie- und Modulationslehre (1906) and Handbuch der Harmonie- und Modulationslehre (1913, 1920).
entries.core_content: Practical multi-voice harmony and modulation handbook in the Max Hesse series (distinct from the larger Breitkopf & Haertel Handbuch der Harmonielehre, HR-T07).

entries.title: Katechismus der Phrasierung (1890) -> Vademecum der Phrasierung (1900, 1912)
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesse, 1890 (with Carl Fuchs); 2nd ed. as Vademecum der Phrasierung, 1900; 3rd ed. 1912.
entries.core_content: Compact reference codifying Riemann's simplified mature phrasing-sign and Lesezeichen system.

entries.title: Katechismus / Handbuch der Fugen-Komposition: Analyse von J. S. Bachs 'Wohltemperiertem Klavier' (Vols. 1-2) und 'Kunst der Fuge' (Vol. 3)
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesse, 1890-1894 (later eds. 1906, 1914-1917, 1920-1921); English trans. J. S. Shedlock, Analysis of J. S. Bach's Wohltemperirtes Clavier, London: Augener, 1893.
entries.core_content: Complete measure-by-measure harmonic, formal, metric, and contrapuntal analysis of all 48 Preludes & Fugues of Bach's WTC plus The Art of Fugue.

entries.title: Katechismus der Musik-Aesthetik (Wie hoeren wir Musik?) (English trans. H. Bewerunge: Catechism of Musical Aesthetics, 1895)
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesse, 1890; English trans. Rev. H. Bewerunge, London: Augener, 1895.
entries.core_content: Accessible handbook presentation of Riemann's cognitive-formalist musical aesthetics.

entries.title: Katechismus der Akustik (Musikwissenschaft) -> Handbuch der Akustik
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesse, 1891; later eds. as Handbuch der Akustik (1914, 1921).
entries.core_content: Acoustic physics, temperament ratios (Pythagorean, just 5-limit, equal temperament), syntonic comma, and tone physiology.

entries.title: Katechismus der Gesangskomposition (Vokalmusik) -> Handbuch der Gesangskomposition
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesse, 1891; later eds. 1912, 1921.
entries.core_content: Systematic prosody, text-setting, declamation, and vocal-polyphonic composition (Lied, choral song, duet, motet).

entries.title: Anleitung zum Partiturspiel (1902; English: Introduction to Playing from Score, 1904) & Katechismus / Handbuch der Orchestrierung (1902)
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesse, 1902 (Partiturspiel: later ed. 1911; English trans. Augener, 1904; Orchestrierung: later eds. 1919, 1921).
entries.core_content: Companion manuals on multi-clef orchestral score reduction and systematic orchestration.

entries.title: Phrasierungsausgaben (Phrasing Editions of Mozart, Beethoven, Bach, Chopin, Field, Rameau, et al.)
entries.publication_details: Leipzig/Berlin/London: Simrock, Steingraeber, Augener, 1883-1890s (beginning Oct. 1, 1883 with Mozart Piano Sonatas Vol. 1 dedicated to Hans von Buelow; over 70 editions total).
entries.core_content: Performance-analytical editions explicitly annotating motive boundaries, metric bar-line realignments, and agogic/dynamic phrasing across the canonical keyboard repertory.

entries.title: Beethovens Streichquartette
entries.publication_details: Berlin: Schlesinger (R. Lienau), 1910 (consolidated from Riemann's Musikfuehrer analytical monographs).
entries.core_content: Complete formal, thematic, and harmonic-functional analysis of Beethoven's string quartets.

entries.title: L. van Beethovens saemtliche Klavier-Solosonaten: Aesthetische und formal-technische Analyse mit historischen Notizen (3 Volumes, 1918-1919)
entries.publication_details: Berlin: Max Hesse, 1918-1919 (3 vols.; 2nd ed. 1920).
entries.core_content: Final grand analytical monument applying mature Riemannian metric numbering (8-bar schemas, hypermetric re-barring) and functional harmony to all 32 Beethoven piano sonatas.

entries.title: Sinfonien der pfalzbayerischen Schule (Mannheimer Symphoniker), 3 Volumes (1902, 1906, 1907)
entries.publication_details: Denkmaeler der Tonkunst in Bayern (DTB), Vols. III/1 (1902), VII/2 (1906), VIII/2 (1907), Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel (Stamitz, Richter, Filtz, Holzbauer, Cannabich, Toeschi, Beck, Eichner).
entries.core_content: Pioneering archival rediscovery and critical edition of the Mannheim orchestral school as precursor to Viennese Classical symphonic form.

entries.title: Mannheimer Kammermusik des 18. Jahrhunderts, 2 Volumes (1914-1915)
entries.publication_details: Denkmaeler der Tonkunst in Bayern (DTB), Vols. XV (1914) & XVI (1915), Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel.
entries.core_content: Critical edition of 18th-century Mannheim chamber repertoire completing Riemann's archival documentation of the school.

entries.authors: Hugo Riemann (ed., with A. Einstein & A. Sandberger for Steffani)
entries.title: Ausgewaehlte Werke von Agostino Steffani (DTB, 1905-1912) & Ausgewaehlte Werke von Johann Schobert (DDT Bd. 39, 1909)
entries.publication_details: Steffani: DTB VI/2, XI/2, XII/2 (Breitkopf & Haertel, 1905-1912); Schobert: Denkmaeler Deutscher Tonkunst Bd. 39 (Breitkopf & Haertel, 1909).
entries.core_content: Critical monument editions documenting Baroque vocal chamber duets (Steffani) and pre-Classical keyboard-chamber style (Schobert).

entries.title: Collegium Musicum (1903-) & Musikgeschichte in Beispielen (1912; later ed. Arnold Schering, 1921)
entries.publication_details: Collegium Musicum: Auswahl aelterer Kammermusikwerke fuer den praktischen Gebrauch (Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel, 1903-); Musikgeschichte in Beispielen (150 compositions, 13th-18th c., Leipzig: Seemann 1912 / Breitkopf & Haertel 1921).
entries.core_content: Practical historical performance series linked to Riemann's 1908 Leipzig Collegium Musicum seminar plus a 150-work historical anthology.

entries.title: Early Vocal & Polyphonic Editions: Binchois Chansons (1892), Illustrationen zur Musikgeschichte (1893), Hausmusik aus alter Zeit (1906), Kantaten-Fruehling (1912)
entries.publication_details: Binchois: Sechs bisher nicht gedruckte dreistimmige Chansons (Wiesbaden, 1892); Illustrationen (Brandstetter, 1893); Hausmusik aus alter Zeit (Breitkopf & Haertel, 1906); Kantaten-Fruehling 1633-1682 (Siegel, 1912).
entries.core_content: Transcriptions of 14th-17th century vocal polyphony and early Baroque cantatas into modern notation.

entries.authors: Alexander Wheelock Thayer (trans. Hermann Deiters; completed & revised by Hugo Riemann)
entries.title: Ludwig van Beethovens Leben (Vols. IV-V completed 1907-1908; Vols. II-III rev. 1910-1911; Vol. I rev. 1917)
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel, 1907-1917 (verified in NDB 21, 2003).
entries.core_content: Riemann completed Volumes IV-V after Hermann Deiters's death and revised Volumes I-III of Thayer's foundational Beethoven biography.

entries.title: Major Theoretical & Orchestration Revisions/Translations: A. B. Marx (1887-90), F.-A. Gevaert (1887, 1891), Ch.-M. Widor (1904)
entries.publication_details: A. B. Marx, Die Lehre von der musikalischen Komposition, rev. H. Riemann (Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel, 1887-90); F.-A. Gevaert, Neue Instrumenten-Lehre (1887) & Der Ursprung des roemischen Kirchengesanges (1891); Ch.-M. Widor, Die Technik des modernen Orchesters (Leipzig, 1904).
entries.core_content: Cross-national transmission of French orchestration and chant scholarship alongside critical revision of Adolf Bernhard Marx's composition treatise.

entries.title: Riemann-Festschrift: Gesammelte Studien. Hugo Riemann zum sechzigsten Geburtstage ueberreicht von Freunden und Schuelern
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Max Hesses Verlag, 1909 (xl + 524 pp.), incl. 'Hugo Riemann: Eine biographische Skizze nebst einem Verzeichnis seiner Werke' (pp. vii-xl, cataloging 58 books + systematic index of essays, editions, and compositions through 1909) and Richard Muennich's study of Riemann's harmony (pp. 60-76).
entries.core_content: Most authoritative contemporaneous primary worklist and biographical document compiled during Hugo Riemann's lifetime.

entries.title: Tentamen novae theoriae musicae ex certissimis harmoniae principiis dilucide expositae (Enestroem E33)
entries.publication_details: St. Petersburg: Typographia Academiae Scientiarum, 1739 (263 pp.).
entries.core_content: Introduces the prime-factor consonance measure (gradus suavitatis) and the earliest 2D lattice representation of pitch-class ratios in powers of 3 and 5 — historical ancestor of Oettingen's and Hugo Riemann's Tonnetz.

entries.title: De harmoniae veris principiis per speculum musicum repraesentatis (Enestroem E457)
entries.publication_details: Novi Commentarii Academiae Scientiarum Petropolitanae 18 (1774, presented 1773), pp. 330-353; Opera Omnia Ser. III, Vol. 1, pp. 568-587.
entries.core_content: Formalizes the 12-tone Speculum Musicum lattice of fifths (3:2) and major thirds (5:4), directly foreshadowing the geometric Tonnetz.

entries.title: Die Natur der Harmonik und der Metrik: Zur Theorie der Musik (English trans. W. E. Heathcote, 1888)
entries.publication_details: Leipzig: Breitkopf & Haertel, 1853 (xii + 394 pp.); English trans. William E. Heathcote, London: Swan Sonnenschein, 1888.
entries.core_content: Hegelian-dialectical derivation of major/minor triads (Einheit/Zweiheit/Verbindung: having vs. being a fifth and third) and symmetric metric organization; foundational philosophical precursor to Hugo Riemann's dualism and metrical theory.

entries.title: Harmoniesystem in dualer Entwickelung: Studien zur Theorie der Musik
entries.publication_details: Dorpat & Leipzig: W. Glaeser, 1866 (revised 2nd ed. Das duale Harmoniesystem, Leipzig: C. F. W. Siegel, 1913).
entries.core_content: Physicist's systematic dual harmony theory introducing Tonicity (common fundamental -> major) vs. Phonicity (common overtone -> minor) and the 2D Tonnetz table of fifths and thirds that catalyzed Hugo Riemann's career in 1871.

entries.title: A Formal Theory of Generalized Tonal Functions
entries.publication_details: Journal of Music Theory 26(1) (Spring 1982), pp. 23-60.
entries.core_content: Axiomatizes 'Riemann systems' as ordered algebraic triples (tonic, dominant-interval, mediant-interval) generalizing T/S/D functional networks beyond classical diatonic tonality.

entries.title: Generalized Musical Intervals and Transformations
entries.publication_details: New Haven: Yale University Press, 1987 (ISBN 978-0-300-03493-6; repr. Oxford University Press, 2007).
entries.core_content: Establishes Generalized Interval Systems (GIS = (S, IVLS, int)), transformational networks, contextual inversions, and simply transitive group actions — founding modern transformational and Neo-Riemannian theory.

entries.title: Some Remarks on the Use of Riemann Transformations
entries.publication_details: Music Theory Online 0(9) (July 1994).
entries.core_content: Demonstrates the exact algebraic relationship and analytical consequences of distinguishing Hugo Riemann's dualist Schritt/Wechsel group (S/W) from non-dualist Rameau-style root transformations and Neo-Riemannian P/L/R operators.

entries.title: Reimag(in)ing Riemann
entries.publication_details: Journal of Music Theory 39(1) (Spring 1995), pp. 101-138 (building on Ph.D. diss., Yale Univ., 1989).
entries.core_content: Proves that the Neo-Riemannian transformations P (Parallel), L (Leittonwechsel), and R (Relative) — with L and R alone sufficient as generators — generate a group of order 24 isomorphic to the dihedral group D_12 acting simply transitively on the 24 consonant triads, represented on the toroidal Tonnetz.

entries.title: Maximally Smooth Cycles, Hexatonic Systems, and the Analysis of Late-Romantic Triadic Progressions
entries.publication_details: Music Analysis 15(1) (1996), pp. 9-40.
entries.core_content: Formalizes the 6-triad maximally smooth hexatonic cycle generated by alternating P and L involutions (LP/PL), partitioning the 24 consonant triads into 4 co-hexatonic systems.

entries.title: Neo-Riemannian Operations, Parsimonious Trichords, and Their 'Tonnetz' Representations
entries.publication_details: Journal of Music Theory 41(1) (1997), pp. 1-66.
entries.core_content: Proves a combinatorial uniqueness theorem: among all trichord set classes in Z_12, consonant triads (sc 3-11, [037]) are mathematically unique in admitting three distinct parsimonious voice-leading involutions (P, L, R), independent of acoustic overtones.

entries.title: Introduction to Neo-Riemannian Theory: A Survey and a Historical Perspective
entries.publication_details: Journal of Music Theory 42(2) (Autumn 1998, Special Neo-Riemannian Issue), pp. 167-180.
entries.core_content: Canonical survey explicitly delineating what Neo-Riemannian theory inherits from Hugo Riemann (contextual transformations, Tonnetz geometry, dualistic symmetry) versus what it strips away (diatonic tonal centricity and 19th-century acoustic dualism).

entries.title: Parsimonious Graphs: A Study in Parsimony, Contextual Transformations, and Modes of Limited Transposition
entries.publication_details: Journal of Music Theory 42(2) (Autumn 1998), pp. 241-263.
entries.core_content: Constructs canonical voice-leading Cayley/parsimony graphs: the Chicken-Wire Torus (dual of the 12-TET Tonnetz), Cube Dance (incorporating augmented triads), and Power Towers (for seventh chords).

entries.title: Some Aspects of Three-Dimensional Tonnetze
entries.publication_details: Journal of Music Theory 42(2) (Autumn 1998), pp. 195-206.
entries.core_content: Generalizes the 2D triadic Tonnetz to a 3D tetrahedral lattice (3-torus T^3) modeling parsimonious transformations among dominant and half-diminished seventh chords.

entries.title: Uniform Triadic Transformations
entries.core_content: Unifies all mode-uniform triadic operators into the UTT group of order 288 (wreath product Z_12 wr Z_2), proving that both the transposition/inversion group T/I and Hugo Riemann's Schritt/Wechsel (PLR) group sit inside UTT as distinct order-24 subgroups.

entries.title: Generalized Contextual Groups
entries.publication_details: Music Theory Online 11(3) (August 2005).
entries.core_content: Generalizes the Schritt/Wechsel (L/R) group to arbitrary ordered pitch-class segments in Z_m (for any modulus m, not only Z_12), proving its exact group-theoretic duality to the T/I group.

entries.authors: Alissa S. Crans, Thomas M. Fiore, & Ramon Satyendra
entries.title: Musical Actions of Dihedral Groups
entries.publication_details: The American Mathematical Monthly 116(6) (June-July 2009), pp. 479-495. doi:10.1080/00029890.2009.11920965; arXiv:0711.1873 [math.GR].
entries.core_content: Clean group-theoretic theorem proving that the T/I group H_1 and the Neo-Riemannian PLR (Schritt/Wechsel) group H_2 are two embedded copies of D_12 inside Sym(24) that are each other's exact centralizer: C_{Sym(24)}(H_1) = H_2 and C_{Sym(24)}(H_2) = H_1.

entries.title: Method and Motivation in Hugo Riemann's History of Harmonic Theory (1992) & Harmonic Function in Chromatic Music (1994)
entries.publication_details: Burnham: Music Theory Spectrum 14(1) (1992), pp. 1-14; Harrison: Chicago & London: University of Chicago Press, 1994.
entries.core_content: Foundational modern historiography and formal rehabilitation of Hugo Riemann's harmonic function theory (scale-degree functional discharges and dualist chromaticism).

entries.title: The 'Table of Relations' and Music Psychology in Hugo Riemann's Harmonic Theory (1996) & Hugo Riemann (1849-1919): Leben, Werk und Wirkung (1999; NDB 21, 2003)
entries.publication_details: Mooney: Ph.D. diss., Columbia University, 1996; Arntz: Cologne: Concerto-Verlag, 1999 & Neue Deutsche Biographie 21 (2003), pp. 592-594.
entries.core_content: Definitive archival biography (Arntz) and primary study tracing Hugo Riemann's Table of Relations (Tonnetz) and its psychological evolution (Mooney).

entries.authors: Alexander Rehding (2003) & Edward Gollin & Alexander Rehding, eds. (2011)
entries.title: Hugo Riemann and the Birth of Modern Musical Thought (2003) & The Oxford Handbook of Neo-Riemannian Music Theories (2011)
entries.publication_details: Rehding: Cambridge University Press, 2003 (doi:10.1017/CBO9780511481369); Gollin & Rehding (eds.): Oxford University Press, 2011 (doi:10.1093/oxfordhb/9780195321333.001.0001; incl. Gelbart & Rehding pp. 140-165 on Folkloristische Tonalitaetsstudien).
entries.core_content: Authoritative modern intellectual biography of Hugo Riemann (Rehding 2003) and the comprehensive Oxford Handbook bridging historical Riemann scholarship with modern algebraic/geometric Neo-Riemannian theories.

entries.title: Musiktheorie als Kompositionslehre und Komposition(slehre) als Musiktheorie - Hugo Riemann zwischen Theorie und Praxis
entries.publication_details: Zeitschrift der Gesellschaft fuer Musiktheorie (ZGMTH) 9(2) (2012), pp. 259-278. doi:10.31751/686.
entries.core_content: Peer-reviewed analysis of how Hugo Riemann bridged abstract music theory and compositional pedagogy across his Handbuecher and Grosse Kompositionslehre.

entries.authors: Dmitri Tymoczko (2006) & Clifton Callender, Ian Quinn, & Dmitri Tymoczko (2008)
entries.title: The Geometry of Musical Chords (Science, 2006) & Generalized Voice-Leading Spaces (Science, 2008)
entries.publication_details: Tymoczko: Science 313(5783) (2006), pp. 72-74 (doi:10.1126/science.1126287); Callender, Quinn, & Tymoczko: Science 320(5874) (2008), pp. 346-348 (doi:10.1126/science.1153021).
entries.core_content: Constructs continuous voice-leading quotient orbifolds (T^n / S_n under OPTIC equivalences) endowed with Euclidean/Riemannian metric geometry (Tradition B), showing how discrete Neo-Riemannian triadic graphs (Tradition C) embed into continuous manifold quotients without conflating the two lineages.

entries.title: A Geometry of Music (2011), The Generalized Tonnetz (JMT, 2012), & Generalized Tonnetze and Zeitnetze (J. Math. Music, 2020)
entries.publication_details: Tymoczko: A Geometry of Music (Oxford Univ. Press, 2011) & 'The Generalized Tonnetz', Journal of Music Theory 56(1) (2012), pp. 1-52 (doi:10.1215/00222909-1546958); Yust: 'Generalized Tonnetze and Zeitnetze, and the Topology of Music Concepts', Journal of Mathematics and Music 14(2) (2020), pp. 170-203 (doi:10.1080/17459737.2020.1725667).
entries.core_content: Establishes exact geometric duality between discrete Tonnetz triangulations and continuous orbifold voice-leading spaces, and extends Tonnetz simplicial/toroidal topology to rhythmic-metric Zeitnetze (unifying Hugo Riemann's harmonic and rhythmic traditions mathematically).
